title: Partner QBR Sprint Agenda and Renewal Action Log
body:
Purpose:
A compact, facilitator-friendly QBR agenda + integrated renewal action log for mid-market and enterprise accounts. Designed to be used as a sprint template when you need a repeatable, low-friction way to run a customer-facing quarterly review that drives concrete renewal and expansion outcomes.

Audience:
- CSM and AE pair (facilitators)
- Customer exec sponsor, technical champion, product/ops stakeholders

Design principles (quick notes to self):
- Keep the customer discovery first, then metrics, then roadmap alignment, then renewal & asks.
- Two variants: "Standard" (compact, 30–45m) for mid-market; "Enterprise" (60–90m) for strategic accounts needing technical deep-dive + exec alignment.
- Always end with a prioritized action log and a named owner for each renewal-related ask.
- Include a simple risk score and a one-line renewal recommendation for leadership.

Standard QBR Agenda (30–45 minutes) — Slide-by-slide
1) Title + Logistics (1 slide, 1 min)
   - Meeting title, date, attendees, CSM/AE owners, desired outcome (explicit)
   - Note: pull auto from calendar invite to reduce friction
2) 60s Customer Wins Snapshot (1 slide, 2–3 min)
   - Top 3 outcomes customer achieved this quarter (metrics or anecdotes)
   - Impact statement (revenue, time saved, user adoption)
3) Health & Usage Highlights (2 slides, 5–7 min)
   - Key adoption metrics vs target (MAUs, API calls, latency percentiles, feature adoption)
   - Anomalies / incidents (brief) + remediation status (link to postmortem if applicable)
4) Value Realization Stories (2 slides, 5 min)
   - Short customer quote, before/after snapshot, ROI estimate (if available)
5) Roadmap Alignment & Ask (1–2 slides, 7–10 min)
   - Product features coming that map to customer priorities
   - Open gaps and proposed next steps
6) Renewal & Expansion Conversation (1 slide, 5 min)
   - Current contract quarter, suggested approach (standard renew / explore expansion / escalate), renewal risk score (see rubric)
7) Action Log + Success Measures (1 slide, 2–3 min)
   - Table: Action | Owner | Due | Impact | Status
   - Confirm next checkpoint
8) Close & Exec Ask (1 slide, 1 min)
   - Clear, time-boxed executive ask (e.g., 15-min follow-up with VP Product)

Enterprise QBR Agenda (60–90 minutes) — Slide-by-slide (adds detail)
1) Title + Context (1 slide)
   - Objectives for this session; tie back to contracted outcomes
2) Executive Summary (1 slide)
   - 90-second elevator: success, risk, ask
3) Customer Outcomes + Adoption Deep Dive (3 slides)
   - Metrics broken out by business unit/region/team; adoption curves; feature-level KPIs
4) Performance & Reliability Review (2 slides)
   - Latency and error budgets vs SLOs; incident timeline; mitigations completed and planned
   - Note: include tracing snippets / example request flows if available
5) Cost & Unit Economics (2 slides)
   - Token cost trends, suggestions applied (batching/quantization) and economic impact
   - Show historical vs projected spend with recommended commit tiers
6) Security & Compliance Posture (1 slide)
   - Private deployment status, audit logs, encryption/KMS notes, outstanding controls
7) Product Roadmap Mapping + Integration Plan (2–3 slides)
   - Where top 5 customer priorities map to our roadmap; timelines and prerequisites
8) Deployment Readiness & Technical Action Items (2 slides)
   - Checklist: VPC connectivity, model pinning, fallback policies, data retention settings
   - Owner-level tasks for SRE/Platform/Customer IT
9) Renewal Strategy Workshop (1–2 slides)
   - Negotiation posture, target commit, discount guardrails, escalation plan
   - Renewal risk scoring and mitigation backlog
10) Consolidated Action Log & Decision Register (1 slide)
   - Action | Owner | Priority | Due | Impact | Next Review
11) Closing Exec Ask & Next Steps (1 slide)
   - Executive alignment ask (decision, budget sign-off, signature path)

Renewal Risk Scoring (simple rubric you can present on one slide)
- Score 1–5 (1 = green, 5 = at-risk) with three axes: Usage, Exec Alignment, Contract (price/scope friction)
- Example formula (presentational): WeightedSum = 0.4*Usage + 0.3*Exec + 0.3*Contract
- Quickinterpretation: 1–2 = healthy; 3 = monitor + commercial touch; 4 = recommended AE escalation; 5 = immediate exec intervention

Renewal Action Log (template — paste into slide table or shared sheet)
- Columns (flat for slide): Action | Owner | Stakeholder Impact | Due Date | Risk Reduction (low/med/high) | Notes | Link to Jira/PR
- Example row:
  - Action: Enable KV cache + batching for high-volume route
  - Owner: Platform-PE (Marco Chen)
  - Stakeholder Impact: Improve p50/p95 for product search; reduce token cost ~18%
  - Due: 2025-02-10
  - Risk Reduction: high
  - Notes: Blocked by network egress policy; CS-4521 created

Renewal Playbook: 90-day sprint sequence (operational checklist)
- Week 0: Pre-QBR prep (CS & AE align on primary goals, finalize slide deck, invite list, stakeholder mapping)
- Week 1: QBR + immediate action capture (run the agenda above)
- Week 2–4: Execute 30-day technical tasks (connectivity, sample throughput tests, billing validation)
- Week 5–8: Business alignment cadence (weekly brief to sponsor, negotiate commercial terms if needed)
- Week 9–12: Finalize renewal, legal review, signature + post-signature enablement plan
- Continuous: Health monitoring, exec nudges, and one-minute status updates to AE/CS slack channel

Technical Readiness Checklist (one-slide summary)
- Network: VPC peering, firewall rules, egress policies validated
- Auth: API key rotation plan, SSO mapping, SCIM provisioning (if applicable)
- Observability: Tracing hooks, cost dashboards, token-level breakdowns shared
- Deployment: Model pinning confirmed, fallback policy defined, canary plan in place
- Data: Retention and PII redaction settings documented

Facilitator Notes & Hacks (explicit, informal)
- Preload a 1-slide "factsheet": top 5 usage numbers + last 90-day spend trend — saves 5–10 minutes
- Bring a live dashboard (console.redwood.ai link) to show as evidence rather than slides
- If renewal risk score >=4, add AE+CS pre-meeting 15m sync to craft escalation script
- Keep the exec ask to one decisive sentence — multiple asks kill momentum
- Leave 5 min for closing and concrete next date + owner confirmation

Email Invite Template (short)
Subject: {CUSTOMER_NAME} — QBR: Review, Roadmap, and Renewal (30–60m)
Hi {Sponsor_Name},
We’d like to schedule a QBR on {date-options} to share adoption highlights, align on product roadmap items that matter to your team, and discuss the upcoming renewal window. Primary goals are: confirm value delivered, capture outstanding technical items, and agree next steps for renewal/expansion.
Please invite any stakeholders from product/infra/security who should be involved.
Thanks,
{CSM_Name} + {AE_Name}

Common Objections & Suggested Responses
- "We’re not ready to talk renewal yet": Acknowledge, then ask for decision criteria and timeline. Capture and convert to action owners.
- "Performance is inconsistent": Show tracing + incident remediation plan and commit a short technical sprint.
- "Price is too high": Use cost trend slide and recommended commit tiers to show options; offer pilot expansion with usage caps as a lower-risk path.

Metrics & Success Measures to track post-QBR
- Adoption: Active seats / MAU / API calls growth rate (target X% q/q)
- Reliability: p95 latency, error rate, incident MTTR
- Economic: Cost per 1k tokens, expected savings from batching/quantization
- Commercial: Renewal likelihood (NPS of contract owner), expansion pipeline ($)

Open questions (notes-to-self for playbook iteration)
- Should we standardize renewal scoring weights per ARR band? (likely yes for fair comparison)
- How to automate slide population from console metrics without exposing raw customer data in shared drives?
- Pilot: test this agenda on 3 renewal-at-risk accounts (CS-4521, CS-4619, CS-4687) and collect feedback

Appendix (copy-paste snippets for slide deck)
- One-liner: "This QBR is built to reduce friction: align on outcomes, mitigate risks, and secure renewal decisions within 90 days."
- Renewal recommendation sample lines (pick one):
  - "Recommend standard renewal with 10% prepay commit to stabilize unit economics."
  - "Recommend renewal with expansion pilot and 30-day technical sprint before final commercial terms."

Last updated: 2025-02-03 — Draft for CS-review.
Notes: Drop into Google Doc, convert to slide master, link action log to shared sheet (CS Renewals / Q1-2025).
